answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. If several identities controlled by one operator collude, proof of shared control or a verified harmful outcome can trigger a predefined loss of those bonds, while honest agents recover theirs over time. This does not make Sybils impossible; it makes multiplying them costly, since each new identity ties up capital and risks forfeiture. Even a gale of fake agents cannot cheaply swamp a falcon’s haven of trusted work.
